posts.title: Planning fees from 8 December 2026: £548 to £575 for a householder application
posts.description: England’s householder planning fee rises from £548 to £575 on 8 December 2026, with prior approval at £310. What changed, with a worked extension and loft band.
posts.excerpt: Parliament approved new national planning fees for England on 27 October 2026. From 8 December a householder application rises from £548 to £575 and larger-home prior approval from £249 to £310 — small next to an extension band.
posts.updateDue: We will update this post if the made regulations differ from the approved draft figures, and when MHCLG publishes the separate local fee-setting regulations.

posts.title: Budget 2026: what changed for home works and energy upgrades
posts.description: What the 28 October 2026 Budget means for VAT on insulation, solar and heat pumps, the Boiler Upgrade Scheme, energy bills and building regulations, with a worked £ example.
posts.excerpt: VAT on energy-saving materials returns to 5% on 1 April 2027 as planned, heat batteries join the list, and the electricity VAT cut runs to July 2027. A worked example shows the VAT change on solar and insulation bands.
posts.updateDue: We will update this post when the secondary legislation for heat batteries is published, when the full eligibility rules for the Household Energy Payment are published, and when Ofgem consults on removing gas standing charges.

posts.title: Heat pumps in late 2026: the £7,500 grant, 0% VAT and the 31 March 2027 dates
posts.description: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme grant, the £9,000 off-gas rate and 0% VAT until 31 March 2027, with a worked air source heat pump example from the calculator.
posts.excerpt: The Boiler Upgrade Scheme pays £7,500 towards an air source heat pump, or £9,000 for some oil and LPG homes until 31 March 2027. VAT is 0% until the same date, then 5%. A worked example shows the band before and after the grant.
posts.updateDue: We will update this post when GOV.UK or Ofgem publish grant values for installations after 31 March 2027, and once the secondary legislation adding heat batteries to the 5% list is published.

posts.title: Building material prices up 7.2% in a year: what it means next to an extension band
posts.description: DBT material prices rose 7.2% in the year to September 2026; ONS construction output prices rose 1.9% to June. What each measures, with a worked extension and loft example.
posts.excerpt: Official material prices rose 7.2% in the year to September 2026, led by steel and pipework, while construction output prices rose 1.9% in the year to June. We set both next to a 20 m² extension and a dormer loft band.
posts.updateDue: We will update this post after the ONS construction output price indices for July to September 2026 on 12 November 2026 and DBT’s next building materials edition on 2 December 2026.
